Definition: a seat; figuratively, a site; abstractly, a session; by extension an abode (the place or the time); by implication, population
BiblicalUsage: Moshav is a dwelling, a seat, a place where people sit and live. Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful, and the sojourning of Israel in Egypt is four hundred and thirty years, and the Sabbath is a holy convocation in all your dwellings.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe where I sit decides who I become. The seat of the scornful and the house of God are both dwellings, and I choose my seat every day.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
